title: M/s Goyal Product Pvt. Ltd. v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sunita Agarwal, J.; Saumitra Dayal Singh, J.
disposition: Mandamus issued to grant temporary connection under Clause 4.10(e) within one week.
headnote: A Chief Judicial Magistrate's order on a Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. application that only calls for a preliminary enquiry report from the Superintending Engineer does not justify refusal of a temporary electricity connection. Mandamus issued to Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam to provide connection in accordance with Clause 4.10(e) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, within one week, provided the consumer completes other necessary formalities.
facts: M/s Goyal Product Private Limited applied for a temporary electricity connection from a mixed feeder under Clause 4.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and deposited the charges. The Superintending Engineer of Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam refused the connection on a dispute raised by a private respondent. The licensee said it could not grant supply because the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Basti, had passed an order on that respondent's Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. application. Respondent officers were misdescribed as of Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam.

reusable_constructions.construction: An order of the Chief Judicial Magistrate on a Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. application that merely calls for a preliminary enquiry report from the Superintending Engineer does not justify refusal of a temporary electricity connection under Clause 4.10(e) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

holding_units.topic: temporary connection; 156(3) CrPC preliminary enquiry as alleged bar
holding_units.holding: A pending Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. order that only calls for a preliminary enquiry report from the Superintending Engineer is no justification to deny a temporary electricity connection. Mandamus issued commanding the licensee to provide connection in accordance with Clause 4.10(e) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, within one week, provided the petitioner fulfils the other necessary formalities.

principle_tags.application: The licensee's refusal, founded only on a CJM order calling for a preliminary enquiry under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C., was held no justification to deny Clause 4.10(e) supply.

not_decided.point: Private respondent no.4's dispute and objections to the connection
not_decided.note: Notice issued; listed for October 2020. Connection nonetheless directed against the licensee.
